contraindications: PDE5 inhibitors, severe hypotension, right ventricular infarction, severe aortic stenosis, raised intracranial pressure caution.
exam_traps: Nitrates are contraindicated with sildenafil/tadalafil.
Need nitrate-free interval to reduce tolerance.
Main antianginal effect is decreased preload.
topics.oral_exam_answer: Nitrates release NO, increase cGMP, and relax vascular smooth muscle. They mainly dilate veins, reducing preload and myocardial oxygen demand, and also dilate large coronary vessels. They are used for angina and selected acute cardiac situations. Key adverse effects are headache and hypotension; PDE5 inhibitors are contraindicated.

clinical_cases.title: Nitrate Contraindication
clinical_cases.case_text: A patient with chest pain took sildenafil earlier the same day.
clinical_cases.question: Why are nitrates dangerous?
clinical_cases.expected_answer: PDE5 inhibitors plus nitrates can cause excessive cGMP-mediated vasodilation and severe hypotension.

podcast.script: Compare administration routes, climb the cephalosporin generation ladder, and explain nitrate NO-cGMP venodilation.
summary_points: Nitrates are contraindicated with PDE5 inhibitors.

final_review: IV route is 100%.
Cephalosporins are beta-lactams.
Cefazolin prophylaxis, cefepime Pseudomonas, ceftaroline MRSA.
Nitrates reduce preload and cannot combine with PDE5 inhibitors.

title: Pharmacovigilance / L-Type Calcium Channel Blockers / Contraceptives
learning_goal: Understand drug safety monitoring, compare CCB subclasses, and classify contraception pharmacology.
why_it_matters: Post-marketing safety, cardiac conduction, and estrogen risk are common oral-exam checkpoints.
oral_exam_goals: Define pharmacovigilance terms and purpose.
Compare dihydropyridine and non-dihydropyridine CCBs.
Classify combined, progestin-only, emergency, and non-hormonal contraceptives.

topics.label: Topic A
topics.title: Pharmacovigilance
topics.theory_short: Pharmacovigilance detects, assesses, understands, and prevents adverse drug effects and other drug-related problems.
topics.definition: Pharmacovigilance is the science and activities of drug safety monitoring.
mechanism_steps: Collect adverse event reports.
Detect safety signals.
Assess causality and risk.
Implement risk minimization.
Update warnings, restrictions, or withdraw drugs when needed.

classification.name: ADR
classification.detail: Harmful and unintended response at normal doses.

classification.name: AE
classification.detail: Any undesirable event during treatment, not necessarily causal.

classification.name: Signal
classification.detail: Information suggesting a new causal association or new aspect of known risk.

classification.name: RMP/PSUR
classification.detail: Risk management and periodic safety reporting tools.

clinical_uses: Post-marketing surveillance, regulatory decisions, safer prescribing.
exam_traps: ADR implies suspected causal drug response; AE does not necessarily.
Rare and delayed harms may appear only after approval.
topics.oral_exam_answer: Pharmacovigilance monitors drug safety during clinical use. It detects adverse reactions, evaluates causality, identifies safety signals, and supports risk minimization or regulatory action such as warnings, restrictions, or withdrawal.

topics.label: Topic B
topics.title: L-Type Calcium Channel Blockers
topics.theory_short: L-type calcium channel blockers reduce calcium influx in vascular smooth muscle and/or myocardium.
topics.definition: CCBs inhibit voltage-gated L-type calcium channels.
mechanism_steps: Dihydropyridines mainly relax vascular smooth muscle.
Verapamil and diltiazem depress AV conduction and contractility.
Reduced calcium influx decreases vasoconstriction or cardiac nodal activity.
clinical_uses: Hypertension, angina, Raynaud, SVT rate control for non-DHPs.
adverse_effects: DHP edema, flushing, headache, reflex tachycardia; verapamil/diltiazem bradycardia, AV block, constipation, HF worsening.
contraindications: Avoid verapamil/diltiazem in AV block, bradycardia, HFrEF, and risky combination with beta-blockers.
exam_traps: Verapamil causes constipation and AV block.
Dihydropyridines cause peripheral edema.
Non-DHP plus beta-blocker can be dangerous.
topics.oral_exam_answer: Calcium channel blockers inhibit L-type calcium channels. Dihydropyridines mainly vasodilate and treat hypertension and angina. Verapamil and diltiazem also depress AV conduction and are useful for rate control but may cause bradycardia, AV block, constipation, and worsen heart failure.

topics.label: Topic C
topics.title: Contraceptives
topics.theory_short: Hormonal contraceptives prevent pregnancy mainly by suppressing ovulation, thickening cervical mucus, and altering endometrium.
topics.definition: Contraceptives are drugs or devices used to prevent pregnancy.
mechanism_steps: Combined estrogen-progestin methods suppress FSH/LH and ovulation.
Progestin thickens cervical mucus and causes endometrial atrophy.
Emergency contraception delays or inhibits ovulation.
Copper IUD impairs fertilization through local inflammatory effects.

classification.name: Combined hormonal
classification.detail: Ethinylestradiol plus progestin pills, patch, ring.

classification.name: Progestin-only
classification.detail: Mini-pill, depot medroxyprogesterone, implant, levonorgestrel IUD.

clinical_uses: Pregnancy prevention, cycle control, dysmenorrhea, acne, reduced ovarian/endometrial cancer risk with combined methods.
adverse_effects: VTE, hypertension, nausea, breast tenderness, irregular bleeding, weight gain with depot, bone density concern with depot, heavier bleeding with copper IUD.
contraindications: Estrogen methods: thromboembolism, migraine with aura, estrogen-dependent cancer, severe liver disease, pregnancy.
exam_traps: Progestin-only methods are useful when estrogen is contraindicated.
Combined contraception increases VTE risk.
Emergency contraception is not regular contraception.
topics.oral_exam_answer: Contraceptives include combined hormonal, progestin-only, emergency, and non-hormonal methods. Hormonal methods prevent pregnancy by suppressing ovulation, thickening cervical mucus, and altering endometrium. Combined methods contain estrogen and progestin but increase thromboembolic risk; progestin-only options are useful when estrogen is contraindicated.

clinical_cases.title: Rate Control Combination
clinical_cases.case_text: A patient on metoprolol is started on verapamil and develops marked bradycardia.
clinical_cases.question: What interaction explains this?
clinical_cases.expected_answer: Additive AV nodal depression from beta-blocker plus non-DHP calcium channel blocker.

podcast.script: Define pharmacovigilance, compare calcium channel blocker subclasses, then classify contraceptives and estrogen risks.
summary_points: ADR is causal harm at normal doses.

final_review: Pharmacovigilance finds post-marketing safety signals.
DHP CCBs: edema/reflex tachycardia.
Non-DHP CCBs: bradycardia/AV block.
Combined contraceptives carry estrogen VTE risk.

title: Types of Doses / Treatment of Peptic Ulcer Disease / Nootropic Substances and Cognitive Medications
short_title: Dose Types / Ulcer Therapy / Cognitive Drugs
learning_goal: Differentiate dose types, explain ulcer pharmacotherapy, and classify dementia/cognitive drugs.
why_it_matters: Dose terminology supports safe prescribing while ulcer and dementia drugs are common mechanism-and-toxicity questions.
oral_exam_goals: Define single, daily, therapeutic, toxic, lethal, loading, maintenance, and cumulative doses.
Explain PPI, H2 blocker, antacid, mucosal protectant, misoprostol, and H. pylori therapy.
Classify acetylcholinesterase inhibitors, memantine, and nootropics.

topics.label: Topic A
topics.title: Types of Doses
topics.theory_short: Dose terminology includes single, daily, therapeutic, maximum, toxic, lethal, loading, maintenance, and cumulative dose.
topics.definition: A dose is the amount of medicine administered in a specified way or time.
mechanism_steps: Therapeutic dose produces desired effect.
Maximum dose is highest recommended safe dose.
Toxic and lethal doses produce harm or death.
Loading dose rapidly reaches target concentration and depends on Vd.
Maintenance dose maintains steady state and depends mainly on clearance.

classification.name: Single/daily dose
classification.detail: Amount at one time or per day.

classification.name: Cumulative
classification.detail: Total exposure over time, important for some toxicities.

clinical_uses: Prescribing, loading dose calculation, therapeutic monitoring, cumulative toxicity prevention.
adverse_effects: Dose-related toxicity if maximum or cumulative dose is exceeded.
exam_traps: Loading dose depends mainly on Vd.
Maintenance dose depends mainly on clearance.
Cumulative dose matters for some cytostatics and organ toxicity.
topics.oral_exam_answer: Dose types include single, daily, therapeutic, maximum, toxic, and lethal doses. Important pharmacokinetic doses are loading dose, determined mainly by volume of distribution, and maintenance dose, determined mainly by clearance. Cumulative dose is total exposure over time and can predict toxicity.

topics.label: Topic B
topics.title: Treatment of Peptic Ulcer Disease
topics.theory_short: Peptic ulcer therapy reduces acid, protects mucosa, removes NSAID triggers, and eradicates H. pylori when present.
topics.definition: Peptic ulcer disease is mucosal injury driven mainly by H. pylori, NSAIDs, and acid/pepsin imbalance.
mechanism_steps: PPIs irreversibly block H+/K+ ATPase.
H2 blockers reduce histamine-mediated acid secretion.
Antacids neutralize existing acid.
Sucralfate and bismuth protect mucosa.
H. pylori eradication uses combination antibiotics plus acid suppression.

classification.name: Misoprostol
classification.detail: Prostaglandin analogue for NSAID ulcer prevention; pregnancy contraindication.

classification.name: Antibiotics
classification.detail: Amoxicillin, clarithromycin, metronidazole, tetracycline with bismuth regimens.

clinical_uses: Ulcer healing, GERD, H. pylori eradication, NSAID ulcer prevention.
adverse_effects: PPI infection/mineral concerns with long-term use, H2 tolerance, antacid constipation/diarrhea, misoprostol diarrhea and uterine contraction.
contraindications: Misoprostol is contraindicated in pregnancy.
exam_traps: PPIs are strongest acid suppressants.
H. pylori needs combination therapy.
Bismuth quadruple therapy is useful with resistance concerns or penicillin allergy contexts.
topics.oral_exam_answer: Peptic ulcer treatment reduces acid, protects mucosa, removes NSAID injury when possible, and eradicates H. pylori. PPIs are the strongest acid suppressants. H. pylori requires combination antibiotic therapy, such as PPI-based triple therapy where suitable or bismuth quadruple therapy in resistance or allergy contexts.

topics.label: Topic C
topics.title: Nootropic Substances and Cognitive Medications
topics.theory_short: Cognitive medications are mainly symptomatic dementia drugs: acetylcholinesterase inhibitors and memantine. Evidence for many nootropics is variable.
topics.definition: Cognitive medications aim to improve or stabilize cognition, mainly in dementia.
mechanism_steps: Acetylcholinesterase inhibitors increase CNS acetylcholine.
Memantine blocks pathological NMDA glutamate activity.
Nootropics/vasoactive agents have variable proposed mechanisms and evidence.

classification.name: Nootropics/vasoactive agents
classification.detail: Piracetam, vinpocetine, ginkgo with variable evidence.

clinical_uses: Alzheimer disease, Lewy body/Parkinson dementia for selected agents, moderate-severe Alzheimer disease for memantine.
adverse_effects: Nausea, diarrhea, bradycardia, syncope with cholinesterase inhibitors; dizziness, confusion, constipation with memantine; bleeding interaction concern with ginkgo.
contraindications: Caution in bradycardia, conduction disease, syncope risk, and drug interactions.
exam_traps: Cognitive drugs are symptomatic and do not cure neurodegeneration.
Cholinesterase inhibitors can cause bradycardia and GI symptoms.
Memantine is for moderate-severe Alzheimer disease contexts.
topics.oral_exam_answer: Cognitive medications include acetylcholinesterase inhibitors such as donepezil, rivastigmine, and galantamine, and the NMDA antagonist memantine. They provide symptomatic benefit in dementia but do not cure neurodegeneration. Monitor cholinergic adverse effects, especially nausea, diarrhea, bradycardia, and syncope.

clinical_cases.title: Syncope On Donepezil
clinical_cases.case_text: An older patient on donepezil develops dizziness and bradycardia.
clinical_cases.question: Which adverse effect explains this?
clinical_cases.expected_answer: Cholinergic enhancement can cause bradycardia and syncope with acetylcholinesterase inhibitors.

podcast.script: Review dose terminology, ulcer treatment logic, and symptomatic cognitive medications.

final_review: Loading dose: Vd. Maintenance dose: clearance.
PUD: PPI plus H. pylori eradication when present.
Misoprostol is contraindicated in pregnancy.
Cholinesterase inhibitors cause GI effects and bradycardia.

title: Drug Allergies / Adrenergic Alpha Receptor Agonists / Classical Anticancer Drugs: Mitotic Poisons and Cytotoxic Antibiotics
learning_goal: Classify immune drug reactions, explain alpha agonists, and know key classical cytostatic mechanisms and toxicities.
why_it_matters: This triplet connects emergency anaphylaxis management, adrenergic receptor logic, and high-risk chemotherapy toxicity.
oral_exam_goals: Classify Gell-Coombs drug allergy types and management.
Compare alpha1 and alpha2 agonists.
Separate mitotic poisons from cytotoxic antibiotics and name key toxicities.

topics.label: Topic A
topics.title: Drug Allergies
topics.theory_short: Drug allergy is immune-mediated and must be separated from predictable toxicity and non-immune intolerance.
topics.definition: Drug allergy is an immune-mediated adverse drug reaction.
mechanism_steps: Type I is IgE-mediated mast cell degranulation.
Type II is IgG/IgM cytotoxic reaction.
Type III is immune complex deposition.
Type IV is delayed T-cell-mediated reaction.
Management begins with stopping the suspected drug and assessing severity.

classification.name: Type IV
classification.detail: Maculopapular rash, contact dermatitis, SJS/TEN, DRESS.

clinical_uses: Allergy documentation, avoidance, desensitization decisions, anaphylaxis treatment.
adverse_effects: Anaphylaxis, severe cutaneous adverse reactions, cytopenias.
contraindications: Do not re-challenge severe reactions such as SJS/TEN, DRESS, or anaphylaxis unless specialist desensitization is essential.
exam_traps: Anaphylaxis treatment is IM adrenaline first.
Allergy is immune-mediated; intolerance is not.
Document reaction clearly, not just 'allergy'.
topics.oral_exam_answer: Drug allergy is immune-mediated and classified as immediate IgE type I, cytotoxic type II, immune-complex type III, and delayed T-cell type IV reactions. Management is stopping the suspected drug, documenting the reaction, symptomatic care, and emergency anaphylaxis treatment with intramuscular adrenaline.

topics.label: Topic B
topics.title: Adrenergic Alpha Receptor Agonists
topics.theory_short: Alpha agonists stimulate alpha1 vasoconstriction and/or alpha2 reduction of sympathetic outflow or transmitter release.
topics.definition: Alpha agonists activate adrenergic alpha receptors.
mechanism_steps: Alpha1 activation causes vasoconstriction and mydriasis.
Central alpha2 activation reduces sympathetic outflow.
Presynaptic alpha2 activation reduces noradrenaline release.
Abrupt alpha2 agonist withdrawal can cause rebound sympathetic activity.
clinical_uses: Hypotension, nasal decongestion, mydriasis, hypertension, withdrawal states, ADHD, sedation.
adverse_effects: Hypertension, reflex bradycardia, ischemia, rebound congestion, sedation, dry mouth, bradycardia, rebound hypertension.
contraindications: Caution in severe hypertension, ischemic disease, bradycardia, and abrupt clonidine withdrawal.
exam_traps: Phenylephrine is pure alpha1 and can cause reflex bradycardia.
Clonidine withdrawal causes rebound hypertension.
Methyldopa is historically important in pregnancy hypertension.
topics.oral_exam_answer: Alpha agonists activate alpha receptors. Alpha1 agonists such as phenylephrine cause vasoconstriction and are used for hypotension, decongestion, and mydriasis. Alpha2 agonists such as clonidine and methyldopa reduce sympathetic outflow and are used in hypertension and selected CNS/autonomic indications. Important risks are rebound hypertension with clonidine withdrawal and rebound congestion with nasal alpha agonists.

topics.label: Topic C
topics.title: Classical Anticancer Drugs: Mitotic Poisons and Cytotoxic Antibiotics
topics.theory_short: Mitotic poisons disrupt microtubules; cytotoxic antibiotics damage DNA by intercalation, topoisomerase inhibition, or free radicals.
topics.definition: Classical cytostatics target rapidly dividing cells and have predictable proliferating-tissue toxicity.
mechanism_steps: Vinca alkaloids inhibit microtubule polymerization.
Taxanes stabilize microtubules and prevent depolymerization.
Etoposide inhibits topoisomerase II.
Anthracyclines intercalate DNA, inhibit topoisomerase II, and generate free radicals.
Bleomycin causes free radical DNA breaks.

classification.name: Cytotoxic antibiotics
classification.detail: Doxorubicin, daunorubicin, bleomycin, dactinomycin, mitomycin C.

clinical_uses: Cancer chemotherapy by tumor protocol.
adverse_effects: Myelosuppression, mucositis, nausea/vomiting, alopecia, infertility, teratogenicity, secondary malignancy; anthracycline cardiotoxicity; bleomycin pulmonary fibrosis; vincristine neuropathy.
contraindications: Organ function and cumulative dose limits vary by drug.
exam_traps: Vinca prevents microtubule polymerization; taxanes prevent depolymerization.
Anthracyclines cause cardiotoxicity.
Bleomycin causes pulmonary fibrosis with little myelosuppression.
topics.oral_exam_answer: Mitotic poisons interfere with microtubules: vinca alkaloids prevent polymerization, while taxanes stabilize microtubules. Cytotoxic antibiotics damage DNA through intercalation, topoisomerase inhibition, or free radicals. Common toxicities are myelosuppression, mucositis, nausea, alopecia, infertility, and teratogenicity, with key specific toxicities such as anthracycline cardiotoxicity and bleomycin pulmonary fibrosis.

clinical_cases.title: Immediate Drug Reaction
clinical_cases.case_text: A patient develops wheeze, hypotension, and urticaria minutes after a beta-lactam injection.
clinical_cases.question: What is first-line emergency treatment?
clinical_cases.expected_answer: Intramuscular adrenaline, plus airway, oxygen, fluids, and adjuncts as needed.

podcast.script: Classify drug allergy, alpha agonists, and classical anticancer drug mechanisms with signature toxicities.

final_review: Drug allergy is immune-mediated.
IM adrenaline treats anaphylaxis.
Alpha1 agonists vasoconstrict.
Vinca blocks microtubule polymerization; taxanes stabilize microtubules.
Doxorubicin cardiotoxicity; bleomycin pulmonary fibrosis.

title: Effects of Drugs on the Fetus / First-Generation Antipsychotics / Androgens
learning_goal: Explain timing-dependent fetal drug toxicity, D2-blocking typical antipsychotics, and androgen pharmacology.
why_it_matters: Pregnancy safety and dopamine pathway adverse effects are high-yield oral exam themes.
oral_exam_goals: Explain pregnancy timing risks and key teratogens.
Map D2 blockade to antipsychotic effects and adverse effects.
Describe androgen receptor action, uses, adverse effects, and contraindications.

topics.label: Topic A
topics.title: Effects of Drugs on the Fetus
topics.theory_short: Fetal drug effects depend on gestational age, dose, duration, placental transfer, maternal metabolism, and fetal elimination.
topics.definition: Fetal drug toxicity is drug-induced harm to embryo, fetus, or neonate.
mechanism_steps: Preimplantation exposure can cause all-or-none death or survival.
Organogenesis has highest malformation risk.
Fetal period causes growth and functional toxicity.
Peripartum exposure can cause neonatal toxicity or withdrawal.
clinical_uses: Pregnancy prescribing, teratogen avoidance, risk counseling.
adverse_effects: Malformations, fetal renal injury, CNS toxicity, teeth/bone toxicity, bleeding, neonatal withdrawal.
contraindications: Known teratogens such as isotretinoin, thalidomide, valproate, methotrexate; ACE inhibitors/ARBs; warfarin; tetracyclines; late NSAID use.
exam_traps: Organogenesis is highest malformation risk.
ACE inhibitors and ARBs cause fetal renal injury.
Tetracyclines affect teeth and bone.
topics.oral_exam_answer: Drug toxicity in pregnancy depends mainly on timing. Preimplantation exposure may cause all-or-none effects, organogenesis carries major malformation risk, and later exposure causes growth, functional, or neonatal toxicity. Important fetal-risk drugs include isotretinoin, thalidomide, valproate, methotrexate, ACE inhibitors/ARBs, warfarin, tetracyclines, aminoglycosides, and late NSAIDs.

topics.label: Topic B
topics.title: First-Generation Antipsychotics
topics.theory_short: Typical antipsychotics mainly block D2 receptors. High-potency drugs cause more EPS; low-potency drugs cause more sedation, alpha1, and anticholinergic effects.
topics.definition: First-generation antipsychotics are dopamine D2 receptor antagonists used mainly for psychotic disorders and agitation.
mechanism_steps: D2 blockade in mesolimbic pathway reduces positive symptoms.
D2 blockade in nigrostriatal pathway causes EPS.
D2 blockade in tuberoinfundibular pathway raises prolactin.
H1, alpha1, and M blockade cause sedation, hypotension, and anticholinergic effects.

classification.name: Low potency
classification.detail: Chlorpromazine, levomepromazine; more sedation and anticholinergic/alpha1 effects.

clinical_uses: Schizophrenia, acute psychosis, mania/agitation, antiemesis for selected agents.
adverse_effects: EPS, tardive dyskinesia, hyperprolactinemia, sedation, orthostatic hypotension, anticholinergic effects, neuroleptic malignant syndrome.
contraindications: Caution in Parkinson disease, dementia-related psychosis, severe QT risk, NMS history.
exam_traps: Nigrostriatal D2 blockade causes EPS.
Tuberoinfundibular D2 blockade causes hyperprolactinemia.
NMS presents with rigidity, fever, autonomic instability, and increased CK.
topics.oral_exam_answer: First-generation antipsychotics are D2 antagonists. Mesolimbic D2 blockade reduces positive psychotic symptoms; nigrostriatal blockade causes EPS; tuberoinfundibular blockade causes hyperprolactinemia. High-potency drugs such as haloperidol cause more EPS, while low-potency drugs cause more sedation, hypotension, and anticholinergic effects. Serious toxicity includes neuroleptic malignant syndrome.

topics.label: Topic C
topics.title: Androgens
topics.theory_short: Androgens are steroid hormones acting through nuclear androgen receptors, used mainly for androgen deficiency.
topics.definition: Androgens are steroid hormones that regulate male sexual development, anabolic effects, and erythropoiesis.
mechanism_steps: Androgen enters cell.
Binds intracellular androgen receptor.
Receptor complex regulates gene transcription.
Effects include virilization, anabolic protein synthesis, and erythropoiesis.

classification.name: Danazol
classification.detail: Historical endometriosis use and hereditary angioedema.

clinical_uses: Male hypogonadism, delayed puberty in selected cases, rare catabolic states, hereditary angioedema for danazol.
adverse_effects: Acne, edema, erythrocytosis, infertility, prostate growth, sleep apnea worsening, hepatotoxicity, dyslipidemia, aggression, virilization in women.
contraindications: Prostate or male breast cancer, pregnancy, severe liver disease, uncontrolled heart failure, high hematocrit, severe BPH symptoms.
exam_traps: Exogenous androgens can suppress spermatogenesis and cause infertility.
Anabolic steroids can damage liver and lipid profile.
Monitor hematocrit and prostate context.
topics.oral_exam_answer: Androgens act through nuclear androgen receptors and are used mainly for androgen deficiency. They promote male sexual development, anabolic effects, and erythropoiesis. Adverse effects include virilization, acne, edema, infertility, erythrocytosis, hepatic toxicity, dyslipidemia, and prostate-related problems.

clinical_cases.title: Rigidity And Fever
clinical_cases.case_text: A patient on haloperidol develops fever, rigidity, autonomic instability, and high CK.
clinical_cases.question: What syndrome is this?
clinical_cases.expected_answer: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome; stop the antipsychotic and provide urgent supportive treatment, cooling, and agents such as dantrolene or bromocriptine when indicated.

podcast.script: Explain fetal risk by pregnancy timing, D2 pathway adverse effects, and androgen receptor pharmacology.
summary_points: Androgens can cause infertility and erythrocytosis.

final_review: Pregnancy timing determines toxicity pattern.
Organogenesis: malformations.
Typical antipsychotics: D2 blockade.
NMS is rigidity, fever, autonomic instability, high CK.
Androgens are nuclear receptor drugs.

title: Classification of Adverse Drug Reactions / Anxiolytics / Classical Anticancer Drugs: Alkylating Drugs and Antimetabolites
learning_goal: Classify ADRs, compare anxiolytic groups, and distinguish DNA-damaging from DNA-synthesis-inhibiting anticancer drugs.
why_it_matters: This triplet links adverse reaction classification with dependence-forming anxiolytics and cytotoxic mechanisms.
oral_exam_goals: Classify ADRs A-F.
Compare benzodiazepines, buspirone, SSRIs/SNRIs, hydroxyzine, and beta-blockers.
Separate alkylating agents from antimetabolites and name rescue/toxicity traps.

topics.label: Topic A
topics.title: Classification of Adverse Drug Reactions
topics.theory_short: ADRs can be classified as A augmented, B bizarre, C chronic, D delayed, E end-of-use, and F failure.
topics.definition: Adverse drug reactions are unwanted harmful reactions during normal drug use.
mechanism_steps: Type A is dose-related and predictable.
Type B is unpredictable or idiosyncratic/allergic.
Type C occurs with chronic use.
Type D is delayed.
Type E is withdrawal or rebound.
Type F is therapeutic failure.

classification.name: A - Augmented
classification.detail: Bleeding with anticoagulants, hypoglycemia with insulin.

classification.name: F - Failure
classification.detail: Resistance or interaction reducing drug level.

clinical_uses: ADR reporting, risk prediction, prevention, patient counseling.
exam_traps: Type A is common, dose-dependent, and predictable.
Type B is uncommon and unpredictable.
Withdrawal reactions are Type E.
topics.oral_exam_answer: ADRs are unwanted harmful reactions during normal drug use. Type A reactions are common, dose-dependent, and predictable. Type B reactions are uncommon and unpredictable. Other categories include chronic, delayed, end-of-use withdrawal or rebound, and therapeutic failure reactions.

topics.label: Topic B
topics.title: Anxiolytics
topics.theory_short: Anxiolytics include rapid benzodiazepines, slower chronic antidepressants, buspirone, hydroxyzine, and beta-blockers for performance symptoms.
topics.definition: Anxiolytics reduce pathological anxiety.
mechanism_steps: Benzodiazepines potentiate GABA-A and increase chloride opening frequency.
SSRIs/SNRIs are first-line chronic anxiety drugs.
Buspirone is a partial 5-HT1A agonist with slow onset.
Hydroxyzine blocks H1.
Propranolol reduces peripheral performance anxiety symptoms.

classification.name: Beta-blockers
classification.detail: Propranolol for tremor/tachycardia in performance anxiety.

clinical_uses: Acute anxiety, panic, generalized anxiety disorder, performance anxiety, chronic anxiety disorders.
adverse_effects: Benzodiazepine sedation, falls, tolerance, dependence, withdrawal, respiratory depression with alcohol/opioids; SSRI initial anxiety; hydroxyzine anticholinergic sedation.
contraindications: Avoid benzodiazepine combinations with alcohol/opioids and caution in substance use disorder or elderly patients.
exam_traps: Benzodiazepines act fast but form dependence.
Buspirone does not work immediately.
Beta-blockers treat somatic performance symptoms, not core psychic anxiety.
topics.oral_exam_answer: Anxiolytics include benzodiazepines, buspirone, SSRIs/SNRIs, hydroxyzine, and beta-blockers for performance symptoms. Benzodiazepines are rapid GABA-A positive modulators but cause sedation, tolerance, dependence, withdrawal, and dangerous interactions with alcohol or opioids. SSRIs/SNRIs are preferred for long-term anxiety; buspirone is non-sedating but slow.

topics.label: Topic C
topics.title: Classical Anticancer Drugs: Alkylating Drugs and Antimetabolites
topics.theory_short: Alkylating agents damage DNA directly and are cell-cycle nonspecific; antimetabolites mimic normal metabolites and inhibit DNA synthesis mainly in S phase.
topics.definition: These classical cytostatics kill dividing cells by DNA damage or DNA synthesis blockade.
mechanism_steps: Alkylating drugs crosslink or alkylate DNA.
Platinum compounds form DNA crosslinks.
Folate antagonists inhibit DHFR or thymidylate synthesis.
Pyrimidine and purine analogues disrupt DNA/RNA synthesis.
Normal proliferating tissues are damaged too.
clinical_uses: Cancer chemotherapy by protocol.
adverse_effects: Myelosuppression, mucositis, alopecia, infertility, teratogenicity, hemorrhagic cystitis with cyclophosphamide/ifosfamide, cisplatin nephro/oto/neurotoxicity.
contraindications: Pregnancy and organ dysfunction cautions by drug.
exam_traps: Cyclophosphamide/ifosfamide hemorrhagic cystitis is prevented with mesna.
Methotrexate can require leucovorin rescue.
Cisplatin causes nephrotoxicity, ototoxicity, and severe nausea.
topics.oral_exam_answer: Alkylating agents damage DNA by alkylation and crosslinking and are cell-cycle nonspecific. Antimetabolites mimic normal metabolites and inhibit DNA synthesis mainly in S phase. Common toxicities are myelosuppression, mucositis, alopecia, infertility, and teratogenicity; key traps include mesna for cyclophosphamide/ifosfamide cystitis and leucovorin rescue for methotrexate.

clinical_cases.title: Alcohol Plus Benzodiazepine
clinical_cases.case_text: A patient takes alprazolam with alcohol and becomes very somnolent.
clinical_cases.question: What is the pharmacodynamic risk?
clinical_cases.expected_answer: Additive CNS and respiratory depression from combining benzodiazepines with alcohol.

podcast.script: Classify ADRs, compare anxiolytics, and separate alkylating agents from antimetabolites.

final_review: ADR A: predictable and dose-related.
ADR B: unpredictable.
BZD: rapid but dependence and respiratory depression with alcohol/opioids.
Alkylators damage DNA; antimetabolites block DNA synthesis.

title: Gastrointestinal Side Effects of Drugs / Drugs Affecting Mucociliary Clearance / Basic Classical Penicillin Antibiotics
learning_goal: Recognize common GI drug toxicities, classify cough and mucus drugs, and understand penicillin subclasses and mechanism.
why_it_matters: GI toxicity and antibiotic allergy are common clinical safety issues, while mucociliary drugs require careful symptom matching.
oral_exam_goals: Name drug causes of nausea, diarrhea, constipation, ulcers, hepatotoxicity, and pancreatitis.
Compare expectorants, mucolytics, mucokinetics, hydration/aerosols, and antitussives.
Classify penicillins and explain PBP/transpeptidase inhibition.

topics.label: Topic A
topics.title: Gastrointestinal Side Effects of Drugs
topics.theory_short: Common GI adverse effects include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation, ulceration, bleeding, hepatotoxicity, and pancreatitis.
topics.definition: GI drug adverse effects are drug-induced disturbances of the digestive tract, liver, or pancreas.
mechanism_steps: Drugs can stimulate CTZ or irritate GI mucosa.
Antibiotics can disturb microbiome and cause C. difficile.
Opioids and anticholinergics reduce motility.
NSAIDs reduce prostaglandin mucosal protection.
Some drugs cause hepatocellular injury or pancreatitis.

classification.name: Constipation
classification.detail: Opioids, anticholinergics, iron, calcium channel blockers.

clinical_uses: ADR recognition, medication review, prevention with gastroprotection or dose change.
adverse_effects: Dehydration, bleeding, liver failure, pancreatitis.
exam_traps: NSAIDs cause ulcers by COX-1 prostaglandin loss.
Antibiotic diarrhea includes C. difficile.
Paracetamol overdose causes liver necrosis.
topics.oral_exam_answer: GI adverse effects include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation, ulceration, bleeding, hepatotoxicity, and pancreatitis. Key examples are NSAID ulcers, opioid constipation, antibiotic-associated diarrhea including C. difficile, metformin diarrhea, and paracetamol liver necrosis in overdose.

topics.label: Topic B
topics.title: Drugs Affecting Mucociliary Clearance
topics.theory_short: Mucociliary clearance depends on mucus viscosity, hydration, ciliary function, and cough. Drugs either help remove mucus or suppress dry cough.
topics.definition: These drugs modify airway secretions or cough reflex to improve respiratory symptom control.
mechanism_steps: Expectorants increase bronchial secretion.
Mucolytics reduce mucus viscosity.
Mucokinetics/secretolytics improve transport.
Saline hydration can loosen secretions.
Antitussives suppress dry nonproductive cough.
clinical_uses: Productive cough with thick secretions, dry irritating cough, airway clearance support.
adverse_effects: GI upset, bronchospasm with inhaled mucolytics, sedation/constipation with codeine.
contraindications: Avoid antitussives when mucus must be cleared; caution with codeine and CNS depressants.
exam_traps: N-acetylcysteine is also the antidote for paracetamol toxicity.
Antitussives are for dry cough, not productive mucus retention.
Codeine has opioid adverse effects.
topics.oral_exam_answer: Drugs improving mucociliary clearance include expectorants, mucolytics, mucokinetics, and hydration/aerosols, which make secretions easier to remove. Antitussives suppress dry nonproductive cough but should not be used when mucus needs to be cleared.

topics.label: Topic C
topics.title: Basic Classical Penicillin Antibiotics
topics.theory_short: Penicillins are beta-lactam bactericidal antibiotics that bind PBPs and inhibit peptidoglycan cross-linking.
topics.definition: Penicillins are beta-lactam antibiotics targeting bacterial cell wall synthesis.
mechanism_steps: Bind PBPs/transpeptidases.
Prevent peptidoglycan crosslinking.
Weaken cell wall.
Cause lysis of growing bacteria.

classification.name: Depot forms
classification.detail: Benzathine penicillin G, procaine penicillin G.

classification.name: Penicillinase-resistant
classification.detail: Oxacillin, cloxacillin, nafcillin; MSSA not MRSA.

classification.name: Aminopenicillins
classification.detail: Ampicillin, amoxicillin; often with beta-lactamase inhibitor.

clinical_uses: Streptococci, pneumococci if susceptible, syphilis, MSSA with antistaphylococcal agents, enterococci/Listeria with aminopenicillins, Pseudomonas with antipseudomonal agents.
adverse_effects: Hypersensitivity, rash, diarrhea, C. difficile, candidiasis, seizures at high dose/renal failure, interstitial nephritis.
contraindications: Severe beta-lactam allergy; adjust dose in renal impairment for many agents.
exam_traps: Ampicillin/amoxicillin rash is common in EBV infection.
Oxacillin/cloxacillin treat MSSA, not MRSA.
Penicillins are time-dependent bactericidal drugs.
topics.oral_exam_answer: Penicillins inhibit PBPs and transpeptidation, blocking peptidoglycan cross-linking and causing bacterial lysis. Main groups are natural penicillins, depot forms, penicillinase-resistant penicillins, aminopenicillins, and antipseudomonal penicillins. The main risk is allergy.

clinical_cases.title: Productive Cough
clinical_cases.case_text: A patient with thick sputum asks for codeine to stop coughing.
clinical_cases.question: Why might this be inappropriate?
clinical_cases.expected_answer: Antitussives should be avoided when mucus needs to be cleared; mucolytic or expectorant support is more logical depending on context.

podcast.script: Review GI adverse effect patterns, mucus clearance drugs, and penicillin subclass logic.

final_review: Antibiotics can cause C. difficile diarrhea.
NSAIDs cause ulcer/bleeding risk.
NAC is mucolytic and paracetamol antidote.
Penicillins inhibit PBPs; allergy is key risk.

title: Bioavailability of Drugs / Opioid Analgesics: Opioid Receptor Agonists / Antacids
learning_goal: Understand bioavailability parameters, opioid agonist effects and toxicity, and antacid mechanisms and interactions.
why_it_matters: This triplet links route conversion, life-threatening respiratory depression, and everyday absorption interactions.
oral_exam_goals: Define F, AUC, Cmax, Tmax, first-pass effect, and bioequivalence.
Explain mu receptor opioid effects, uses, adverse effects, and naloxone.
Compare aluminium, magnesium, calcium, bicarbonate, and alginate antacid issues.

topics.label: Topic A
topics.title: Bioavailability of Drugs
topics.theory_short: Bioavailability is the fraction of administered dose reaching systemic circulation unchanged. IV bioavailability is 100%.
topics.definition: Bioavailability, F, is the extent of unchanged drug reaching systemic circulation.
mechanism_steps: Drug is administered by a route.
Absorption may be incomplete.
Gut wall or liver first-pass metabolism may remove drug.
Systemic exposure is reflected by AUC.
Cmax and Tmax describe peak and time to peak.

classification.name: Bioequivalence
classification.detail: Comparable AUC and Cmax between formulations.

clinical_uses: Dose conversion between routes, formulation comparison, first-pass avoidance.
adverse_effects: Low bioavailability can cause therapeutic failure; unexpectedly high bioavailability can cause toxicity.
exam_traps: Absorption and bioavailability are not identical.
IV is 100%.
First-pass metabolism lowers oral bioavailability.
topics.oral_exam_answer: Bioavailability is the proportion of unchanged drug reaching systemic circulation. It is complete after IV administration but often reduced after oral dosing by incomplete absorption and first-pass metabolism. AUC reflects total exposure, Cmax peak concentration, and Tmax time to peak. Bioavailability determines dose conversion between routes.

topics.label: Topic B
topics.title: Opioid Analgesics: Opioid Receptor Agonists
topics.theory_short: Opioid agonists mainly stimulate mu receptors, inhibiting transmitter release and hyperpolarizing neurons. Respiratory depression is the key lethal toxicity.
topics.definition: Opioid agonists activate mu, kappa, and delta opioid receptors; mu is most clinically important.
mechanism_steps: Presynaptic calcium influx decreases.
Neurotransmitter release decreases.
Postsynaptic potassium efflux increases.
Neurons hyperpolarize.
Brainstem CO2 sensitivity falls, causing respiratory depression.

classification.name: Strong agonists
classification.detail: Morphine, fentanyl, sufentanil, oxycodone, hydromorphone, methadone.

clinical_uses: Severe acute/chronic/cancer pain, anaesthesia, MI pain, palliative dyspnea, diarrhea for loperamide.
adverse_effects: Respiratory depression, miosis, constipation, nausea/vomiting, sedation, euphoria, dependence, tolerance, withdrawal, histamine release.
contraindications: Avoid dangerous combination with benzodiazepines, alcohol, and severe respiratory depression context unless carefully managed.
exam_traps: Miosis and constipation develop little tolerance.
Naloxone reverses acute opioid intoxication.
Codeine depends on CYP2D6 activation.
topics.oral_exam_answer: Opioid agonists mainly stimulate mu receptors, inhibit neurotransmitter release, and hyperpolarize neurons, producing strong analgesia. Main adverse effects are respiratory depression, miosis, constipation, nausea, sedation, tolerance, dependence, and withdrawal. Naloxone reverses acute opioid intoxication.

topics.label: Topic C
topics.title: Antacids
topics.theory_short: Antacids are weak bases that neutralize existing gastric acid and provide quick symptom relief but do not strongly suppress acid production.
topics.definition: Antacids neutralize gastric acid already present in the stomach.
mechanism_steps: Weak base reacts with gastric acid.
Intragastric pH rises briefly.
Symptoms may improve quickly.
Chelation or pH change can reduce absorption of other drugs.

classification.name: Calcium carbonate
classification.detail: Constipation, hypercalcemia, acid rebound, milk-alkali syndrome.

clinical_uses: Short-term dyspepsia or reflux symptom relief.
adverse_effects: Constipation, diarrhea, hypercalcemia, alkalosis, electrolyte issues, drug absorption interactions.
contraindications: Renal failure caution for magnesium/aluminium; sodium load caution for bicarbonate.
exam_traps: Antacids reduce absorption of tetracyclines, fluoroquinolones, iron, and levothyroxine.
Separate interacting drugs by several hours.
Magnesium causes diarrhea; aluminium causes constipation.
topics.oral_exam_answer: Antacids neutralize gastric acid and are used for short-term dyspepsia or reflux symptoms. Aluminium causes constipation, magnesium causes diarrhea, calcium may cause hypercalcemia, and sodium bicarbonate can cause alkalosis and sodium load. Antacids commonly impair absorption of other drugs by chelation or pH effects.

clinical_cases.title: Pinpoint Pupils And Slow Breathing
clinical_cases.case_text: A patient has coma, miosis, and respiratory depression after suspected opioid use.
clinical_cases.question: Which antidote is used?
clinical_cases.expected_answer: Naloxone, with airway and ventilation support as needed.

podcast.script: Explain bioavailability curves, opioid agonist toxicity, and antacid interactions.
summary_points: F is unchanged drug reaching systemic circulation.

final_review: Bioavailability: F and AUC.
IV F is 100%.
Opioids: mu agonism, respiratory depression, miosis, constipation.
Naloxone reverses overdose.
Antacids chelate and alter absorption.

title: The Medical Prescription and Its Structure / Treatment of Angina Pectoris / Tetracycline Antibiotics
learning_goal: Know prescription structure, explain angina treatment, and classify tetracycline mechanism, uses, and risks.
why_it_matters: This final early module tests legal prescribing basics, ischemia logic, and one of the most exam-friendly antibiotic classes.
oral_exam_goals: Name patient, prescriber, Rp., subscription, signatura, date, and authentication fields.
Explain acute and preventive angina therapy.
Explain tetracycline 30S mechanism, uses, chelation, teeth/bone toxicity, and contraindications.

topics.label: Topic A
topics.title: The Medical Prescription and Its Structure
topics.theory_short: A prescription is a legal medical document identifying patient, prescriber, medicine, dosage instructions, date, and authentication.
topics.definition: A medical prescription is a legal order for preparation or dispensing of a medicinal product.
mechanism_steps: Identify patient.
Identify prescriber.
Write drug name, strength, dosage form, package size, and amount.
Add dispensing or compounding instructions when needed.
Write signatura: dose, route, frequency, and duration for the patient.
Date and authenticate.

classification.name: Patient data
classification.detail: Name, date of birth/personal ID, address/insurance data as required.

classification.name: Rp./inscription
classification.detail: Drug name, strength, dosage form, package size, amount.

classification.name: Subscription
classification.detail: Instruction to pharmacist for prepared medicine.

clinical_uses: Safe, legal medication dispensing and patient instruction.
adverse_effects: Prescription errors can cause wrong drug, dose, route, frequency, or duration.
exam_traps: Signatura is the patient instruction part.
Prescription is both therapeutic and legal.
Dose, route, frequency, and duration must be clear.
topics.oral_exam_answer: A prescription contains identification of patient and prescriber, the prescribed drug with strength, dosage form and quantity, instructions for dispensing and patient use, date, and authentication. It is both a therapeutic and legal document.

topics.label: Topic B
topics.title: Treatment of Angina Pectoris
topics.theory_short: Angina therapy reduces oxygen demand, improves supply, relieves acute pain, and prevents thrombosis and progression.
topics.definition: Angina pectoris is ischemic chest pain from myocardial oxygen supply-demand imbalance.
mechanism_steps: Nitrates venodilate and reduce preload.
Beta-blockers reduce heart rate and contractility.
Calcium channel blockers vasodilate and/or reduce cardiac work.
Antiplatelets and statins reduce ischemic events and plaque progression.
Other antianginals target late sodium current, heart rate, or metabolism.

classification.name: Nitrates
classification.detail: Nitroglycerin and isosorbide; acute relief and prophylaxis.

classification.name: Beta-blockers
classification.detail: Metoprolol, bisoprolol, atenolol; first-line stable exertional angina.

classification.name: Calcium channel blockers
classification.detail: Verapamil/diltiazem and amlodipine; vasospasm and demand reduction.

clinical_uses: Acute angina attacks, stable angina prophylaxis, vasospastic angina, secondary prevention.
adverse_effects: Nitrate headache/hypotension, beta-blocker bradycardia/bronchospasm/fatigue, CCB edema or AV block, antiplatelet bleeding, statin myopathy.
contraindications: Nitrates with PDE5 inhibitors; beta-blockers alone in vasospastic angina; non-DHP CCBs in AV block/HFrEF.
exam_traps: Acute attack: stop activity, sit, sublingual nitroglycerin; persistent pain needs emergency evaluation.
Nitrates cannot combine with PDE5 inhibitors.
Beta-blockers reduce demand in stable exertional angina.
topics.oral_exam_answer: Angina treatment includes nitrates for acute relief, beta-blockers and calcium channel blockers to reduce oxygen demand or vasospasm, and prognostic therapy with antiplatelets, statins, and risk-factor control. Nitrates reduce preload and myocardial oxygen demand but must not be combined with PDE5 inhibitors.

topics.label: Topic C
topics.title: Tetracycline Antibiotics
topics.theory_short: Tetracyclines bind reversibly to the 30S ribosomal subunit and block aminoacyl-tRNA attachment. Chelation and teeth/bone toxicity are key exam traps.
topics.definition: Tetracyclines are broad-spectrum bacteriostatic protein synthesis inhibitors.
mechanism_steps: Bind reversibly to the 30S ribosomal subunit.
Block aminoacyl-tRNA attachment.
Inhibit bacterial protein synthesis.
Chelate divalent/trivalent cations, reducing absorption.
Accumulate in developing teeth and bone.

classification.name: Tetracycline
classification.detail: Older, shorter acting, affected by food and cations.

classification.name: Doxycycline
classification.detail: Long acting, better absorption, less affected by food; atypicals, chlamydia, rickettsia, borrelia, acne, malaria prophylaxis.

classification.name: Tigecycline
classification.detail: IV glycylcycline, broad but no Pseudomonas.

clinical_uses: Atypical pneumonia, chlamydia, rickettsiae, borrelia, acne, malaria prophylaxis, selected MRSA or complicated infections depending on drug.
adverse_effects: GI irritation, esophagitis, photosensitivity, chelation interactions, teeth discoloration, bone growth inhibition, hepatotoxicity, superinfection, Fanconi-like syndrome with expired tetracycline.
contraindications: Pregnancy and young children; avoid taking with milk, antacids, iron, calcium, magnesium, aluminium around dosing.
exam_traps: Do not take with milk or antacids because of chelation.
Avoid in pregnancy and young children due to teeth/bone toxicity.
Doxycycline is useful for atypicals, rickettsiae, chlamydiae, borrelia, and acne.
topics.oral_exam_answer: Tetracyclines bind the 30S ribosomal subunit and prevent aminoacyl-tRNA binding, inhibiting protein synthesis. They cover atypicals, rickettsiae, chlamydiae, borrelia, and many Gram-positive/negative organisms. Main adverse effects are GI irritation, photosensitivity, chelation interactions, teeth discoloration and bone growth inhibition, so they are avoided in pregnancy and children.

clinical_cases.title: Doxycycline With Milk
clinical_cases.case_text: A patient takes doxycycline with milk and antacids and does not improve.
clinical_cases.question: What pharmacokinetic interaction explains this?
clinical_cases.expected_answer: Chelation with calcium, magnesium, aluminium, or iron reduces tetracycline absorption.

podcast.script: Name prescription parts, explain angina therapy, then summarize tetracycline 30S mechanism, uses, chelation, photosensitivity, and pregnancy/child contraindications.
summary_points: Angina therapy reduces oxygen demand and prevents thrombosis.
Nitrates cannot combine with PDE5 inhibitors.
Avoid tetracyclines in pregnancy and young children.

final_review: Prescription: patient, prescriber, Rp., subscription, signatura, date, authentication.
Angina: nitrates, beta-blockers, CCBs, antiplatelets, statins.
Tetracyclines: 30S, atypicals/rickettsiae/chlamydiae/borrelia/acne.
Avoid milk/antacids, pregnancy, and young children.
